# View

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set view=</code><span class="gp-chip">21 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

The view stage chooses the approach direction of every seed: two of the three degrees of
freedom of the grasp orientation. The grouper crops the scene in the frame it chooses, so it
decides what the head gets to see.

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set view=lattice-view -o graspnet-baseline_lattice-view.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list view
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set view=lattice-view -o gsnet_lattice-view.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list view
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set view=lattice-view -o scale-balanced-grasp_lattice-view.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list view
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set view=lattice-view -o economicgrasp_lattice-view.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list view
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set view=lattice-view -o finegrasp_lattice-view.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list view
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#view) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#view) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#view) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#view) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#view).

## Choosing

- **The labels know 300 directions.** Every option snaps its choice to one of the 300 label
  views for training, so a finer lattice does not give finer labels.
- **Fewer classes:** `lattice-fibonacci-120`, `icosphere-162` or `healpix-192`; only
  approaches away from the camera: `lattice-hemisphere-60`.
- **A classification instead of 300 regressions:** `lattice-best-view`; `lattice-angular-cost`
  makes near misses cheap.
- **No lattice at all:** `direction-regression`, with a confidence `direction-vmf`; a whole
  grasp frame: `two-vector` or `rotation-6d`.
- **The head keeps the in-plane angle.** A stage that regresses a full rotation contributes its
  approach axis; the rest of the frame is supervised and logged, not decoded.

## Details

??? note "Which option for which need"

    | You want | Take | Why |
    |---|---|---|
    | the view scoring of GSNet, EconomicGrasp and FineGrasp | `template-view` | a score per label view; the training view is sampled from the scores |
    | the view stage of GraspNet-baseline or Scale-Balanced-Grasp | `objectness-view`, `objectness-view-graspable` | also predicts objectness, which their heads read |
    | the same scoring as a base for the options below | `lattice-view` | computes what `template-view` computes, on a lattice of any size |
    | a smaller output layer | `lattice-fibonacci-120`, `icosphere-162`, `healpix-192` | fewer classes; each view is supervised by its nearest label view |
    | only approaches away from the camera | `lattice-hemisphere-60` | the 60-of-120 template of RGB Matters |
    | a classification of the best view | `lattice-best-view`, `lattice-angular-cost` | cross-entropy on the most graspable view; the second adds the angular class loss of RGB Matters |
    | a direction between lattice points at inference | `lattice-soft-argmax` | softmax-weighted mean of the best view directions |
    | training crops closer to what inference chooses | `lattice-topk` | samples the training view among the 10 best views |
    | no lattice in the output | `direction-regression`, `direction-vmf` | 3 numbers per seed and a cosine loss; or a von Mises-Fisher likelihood with a concentration |
    | a full grasp frame | `two-vector`, `two-vector-baseline`, `rotation-6d`, `rotation-9d`, `rotation-quaternion` | Gram-Schmidt of two vectors, or the rotation mappings of RoMa |

??? note "Input and output"

    `approach, seeds = view(seeds)`, and `view.loss(approach, matched)` for its own loss.

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | receives | `SeedSet`: `M` seeds of the batch, coordinates `(M, 3)` in metres in the camera frame and features `(M, C)`; `C` is injected (`in_channels`) |
    | returns | `ApproachSet`, one row per seed, and the `SeedSet` (a stage may add a residual to the features, a score, or mark seeds invalid) |
    | `direction` | `(M, 3)` unit vectors; read by the decoder of every head: rotation = `approach_to_rotation(direction, in-plane angle)` |
    | `rotation` | `(M, 3, 3)`, column 0 the direction; the crop frame of the grouper at inference |
    | `view_index` | `(M,)` index into `view.template`, the 300 views the labels are indexed by; the assigner looks the labels up there in training |
    | declares | `label_formats` (dense or compact labels it can read), `needs_matched`, `seed_scores` (scores it adds), `applies_seed_weights` |

    Three facts shape every option:

    1. **The labels know 300 directions.** GraspNet-1Billion and GraspClutter6D labels are
       indexed by a 300-view Fibonacci lattice. A stage may predict on another lattice or
       none, but it snaps its choice to one of those views for the label lookup.
    2. **Train and inference crops differ by the snap.** In training the crop frame is the
       label frame of the snapped view; at inference it is the direction the stage returned.
    3. **The head owns the in-plane angle.** Every head decodes
       `approach_to_rotation(direction, angle bin)`.

    What each kind of stage needs:

    | Stage | From the labels | From the assigner | From the head |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | lattice stages (`Lattice`, `Icosphere`, `Healpix`) | the graspness of all 300 label views per seed (dense or compact) | the label lookup at `view_index` | nothing |
    | `DirectionViewStage` | the same, reduced to the most graspable view | the same | nothing |
    | `TwoVectorViewStage`, `RomaRotationViewStage` | the same, plus the grid or angle bin of the snapped view | also `crop_rotation`, the label frame of the snapped view | the same `num_angle` (checked) |

    No new stage has released weights. A checkpoint of a ported method loaded into a model with
    another view stage leaves only that stage untrained.

??? note "The settings that matter"

    A lattice stage:

    ```yaml
    model:
      view:
        type: LatticeViewStage        # or IcosphereViewStage (subdivisions) / HealpixViewStage (nside)
        num_views: 300
        hemisphere: false             # true: only approaches away from the camera
        target: score                 # score | best_view
        selection: argmax             # inference: argmax | soft_argmax
        train_selection: multinomial  # training: multinomial | topk | argmax
        top_k: null                   # used by soft_argmax and topk
        temperature: 1.0              # softmax temperature of soft_argmax
        angular_weight: 0.0           # best_view only: weight of the angular class loss
    ```

    - **Size.** An icosphere has `10 · 4**subdivisions + 2` views, HEALPix `12 · nside**2`.
      Beyond 300 views neighbouring views share one label column.
    - **`target: score`** regresses the normalised graspness of every view (GSNet's).
      **`target: best_view`** classifies the most graspable view; use it with
      `train_selection: argmax` and a `CrossEntropy` loss.
    - **`selection: soft_argmax`** changes inference only. A temperature of about 0.05 fits
      regressed scores in [0, 1], 1.0 fits logits; keep `top_k` small (8).

    A regression stage:

    ```yaml
    model:
      view:
        type: TwoVectorViewStage
        keep: approach                # approach (6-D order) | baseline (Contact-GraspNet order)
        direction_weight: 1.0         # loss/view: 1 - cos to the most graspable label view
        frame_weight: 1.0             # loss/view_frame: distance to the label frame, half-turn aware
        num_angle: 12                 # must equal the head's
    ```

    - `loss/view_frame` takes the smaller of the distances to the label frame and to its
      half-turn copy: a parallel-jaw grasp turned by 180° about its approach is the same grasp.
    - `representation` of `RomaRotationViewStage`: `6d` and `9d` are continuous; `quaternion`
      and `rotvec` are there for comparison (`rotvec` has no preset and no probe record).
    - `residual: true` adds the hidden features of the stage to the seed features, as GSNet's
      stage does.

    | `LatticeViewStage` | the same scoring on a free lattice; the hemisphere template of RGB Matters ([arXiv 2103.02184](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.02184), ICRA 2021) | written for GraspPanda; the angular class loss adapted from [GouMinghao/rgb_matters@2e176728f6](https://github.com/GouMinghao/rgb_matters/blob/2e176728f6/rgbd_graspnet/net/loss.py) (MIT, see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`) | none |
    | `IcosphereViewStage` | subdivided icosahedron | bridge to [trimesh](https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh) (MIT) | `trimesh` |
    | `HealpixViewStage` | HEALPix (Górski et al., ApJ 2005) | bridge to [healpix](https://github.com/ntessore/healpix) (BSD-3-Clause) | `healpix` |
    | `DirectionViewStage` | the approach network of Generalizing-Grasp ([arXiv 2404.01727](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01727), CVPR 2024); the vMF likelihood of vMF-Contact ([arXiv 2411.03591](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03591), ICRA 2025) | written for GraspPanda (both repositories have no licence file) | none |
    | `TwoVectorViewStage` | the 6-D rotation representation ([arXiv 1812.07035](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.07035), CVPR 2019); the order of Contact-GraspNet ([arXiv 2103.14127](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14127)) | written for GraspPanda (the idea only) | none |
    | `RomaRotationViewStage` | 6-D, 9-D + SVD ([arXiv 2006.14616](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.14616)), quaternion, rotation vector | bridge to [RoMa](https://github.com/naver/roma) (BSD-3-Clause) | `roma` |

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **A finer lattice does not give finer labels.** Angles for 200 000 random directions,
      computed with the lattices of `grasppanda.ops`:

        | Lattice | Views | Random direction to nearest view, mean / max | View to its nearest label view, mean / max | Label columns read |
        |---|---|---|---|---|
        | Fibonacci (the labels) | 300 | 4.5° / 9.0° | 0° | 300 |
        | Fibonacci | 120 | 7.1° / 14.1° | 4.6° / 7.7° | 120 |
        | icosphere | 162 | 6.1° / 10.8° | 4.5° / 7.7° | 162 |
        | icosphere | 642 | 3.0° / 5.4° | 4.5° / 8.1° | 300 |
        | HEALPix | 192 | 5.6° / 11.5° | 4.5° / 7.9° | 190 |
        | HEALPix | 768 | 2.8° / 5.6° | 4.5° / 8.4° | 300 |

        The third column is the price of a coarse lattice; the fourth is the crop mismatch of
        any lattice that is not the label lattice.

    - **`TemplateViewStage(num_views=N)` with N ≠ 300 is not another lattice size.** Its
      template is also the label lattice, so the assigner refuses the labels. Use
      `LatticeViewStage(num_views=N)`.
    - **Soft-arg-max needs a temperature that fits the outputs.** With regressed scores and a
      temperature of 1 the weights are nearly uniform; with every view voting, opposite views
      can cancel (the stage then falls back to the best view).
    - **A single best view is a brittle target.** On a symmetric object two distant views can
      tie and the target flips between them; `target: score` and `angular_weight` suffer less.
    - **Flip augmentation yields mirrored label frames.** The frame loss skips those seeds; their
      direction loss still counts.
    - **The vMF loss is a log-density and goes negative** when the concentration is high.
    - **healpy is GPL-2.0**, so the bridge uses the BSD-licensed `healpix` package.

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | Contact-GraspNet code ([NVlabs/contact_graspnet](https://github.com/NVlabs/contact_graspnet)) | its licence limits use to non-commercial research. Its parameterisation is `two-vector-baseline`; its contact labels need an asset the toolbox does not have. |
    | vMF-Contact, Generalizing-Grasp and S4G code | no licence files. The closed-form likelihood, the cosine regression and the 6-D representation are written here; their other terms are not. |
    | DexGraspNet 2.0 (diffusion on seed features) | no licence file; a generative head is a head, not a view stage. |
    | OrbitGrasp, Edge Grasp Network | detectors of their own with their own simulated labels. |
    | PyTorch3D rotation conversions | a compiled package for functions RoMa has in pure PyTorch. |
    | Several grasps per seed at inference | `ApproachSet` has one row per seed; it needs a change of the skeleton. |
    | A head that takes the regressed in-plane rotation | belongs to the head slot; until it exists the frame of the rotation stages is auxiliary. |
